chapter: The Footlight Club and Washington friends
title: Marty Emerson, Jack Schaeffer and what those associations meant
summary: He names two younger regulars, and says these associations left an indelible mark on his approach to music.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: One of the people who used to come up that I remember is a guy named Marty Emerson, who was a trombone player, him and a guy named Jack Schaeffer, who was a trumpet player. I think Jack Schaeffer went to Las Vegas. I don't know if he's still around or not. But Marty Emerson is now Secretary of the international body of the American Federation of Musicians. If you ever get the International newspaper or have anything to do with the American Federation of Musicians, Marty Emerson is the Secretary, and he's a big wheel there now.

Anyway, those were just some memorable days in shaping, you know, every approach that I had to music. And these associations... You aren't aware of it when they're happening, but they have an indelible stamp on you for life. The big bands and the little band that I had...
